Isis. The goddess of magic, motherhood, and devotion. She used her supernatural powers to resurrect her murdered husband Osiris and conceived their son Horus in secret. She became one of the most widely worshipped goddesses in Egypt and eventually spread throughout the Greco-Roman world as a symbol of feminine power and protection. Depicted as a winged goddess crowned with a throne symbol on her head, Isis was often shown with Horus as an infant at her breast. She performed the first act of magic in Egyptian mythology by using a spell to resurrect her husband Osiris after Set's murder. When she conceived Horus, she concealed herself and her infant son in the papyrus marshes to protect him from Set's vengeance and to give Horus time to grow strong enough to reclaim his father's throne. Isis was the queen of all magic, known as heka, wielding spells to heal, protect, and restore life itself. She was sister and wife of Osiris, sister to both Set and Nephthys, and mother of Horus. She was central to the greatest myth cycle of ancient Egypt. Her devotion to Osiris and maternal protection of Horus made her the ideal model of fidelity and motherhood throughout Egyptian culture. Though worshipped throughout Egypt, her major cult centers were at Philae and Dendera, where her healing and protective powers were especially invoked by the faithful. Over time, her worship spread across the Mediterranean world, and she was adopted into Greco-Roman mystery religions as a universal mother goddess.
